items.title: Wayne Bergeron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2020
items.q: I kept seeing these three names: Jerry Hey, Chuck Findley, and Gary Grant.

ctx.x: So you see, okay here’s Frank Wess with Basie and then you see Frank Wess over here. And here’s Snooky Young here, and then he shows up — and I used to just love watching the musical chairs. And I’m wondering if you were like that, and did you latch on to some of those lead trumpet players?

Most definitely. And more in the pop world, because I would look at all these records and I kept seeing these three names: Jerry Hey, Chuck Findley, and Gary Grant. I mean on every record that I liked, you know, whether it was an Earth, Wind and Fire record or whatever, I would just keep seeing these names. I go man who are these? They’re on everything. And everything they do sounds great too you know. And so when one of them wasn’t there, you know as a kid I’d look at those things and go, “Wow, Chuck Findley’s…
section. You’d go, “Wow, isn’t he with Count Basie? How could he be doing these two gigs at once?”

items.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023
items.q: I call the guys who I think are best for the job and Wayne Bergeron is kind of the guy now who can play anything. So he plays.

ctx.x: Is it tough for you over the years to, you want to send in the Jerry Hey Horns so does that mean that you have to get on the phone with all the members every time you get called for a recording session? To see that they could all make it?

Well you know Gary Grant is not playing anymore so you know he was like a key member of the horn section. Bill Reichenbach has moved to near Asheville, North Carolina, and he’s also another, was a key member. He comes back to play on movies now. He does all the John Williams’ movies and plays on movies but he’s not always here when I do a session. And Larry Williams, who is still playing saxophone but because of a lot of times it’s baritone saxophone now and Dan Higgins plays everything amazingly well so he’s…
I’m sure it’s excellent, and it’s a blessing to have that group of musicians who you’d have to go out of your way to get someone who wasn’t cutting it.
